structured.approach: This attempt fixes the single G1 refusal in feat.fitment. The sentence 'REQ-02 linked the entry to R-AP-12' wrongly said REQ-02 made the link. It now reads: 'feat.classification records R-AP-12 as the entry's linked roadmap item, citing feat.prebacklog as the source of the link.' I searched the file for other statements that credit an action to a step and reworded one more: the ZD-48510 row now says feat.classification marks it 'Not grouped', not 'REQ-02 did not group it'. Nothing else changed: the verdict, reason code, evidence, notification and open questions are the same as in the previous attempt. Inputs used: feat.classification, org.strategy_capability and org.roadmap, plus requirements/ZD-48600.md and REG-LPR-2026-4.2.md for exact wording, and shared memory for decisions.

claims.text: The Q4 2026 AP roadmap contains R-AP-12 'give AP managers earlier visibility of overdue payables', owned by the PM.
feat.classification records R-AP-12 as the entry's linked roadmap item, citing feat.prebacklog as the source of the link.

The ticket says AP managers want to see which overdue invoices belong to vendors that usually pay late, so they can chase them first. It asks for unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due, sorted by days descending then id, each with a risk level.
R-AP-14 is 'aging export for finance close', and none of CR-1 to CR-7 adds an export.
The current capability is ap_aging computing aging buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+) for open invoices. The entry keeps every existing signature and adds new functions.
org.strategy_capability does not mention ap_pipeline, ap_forecast or ap_portal. The ZD-48600 architecture override describes them.
org.strategy_capability states no explicit out-of-scope list.

The feature risk map records 'No finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution in this change' with advisory tier T2. feat.classification marks ZD-48510 (payment execution) 'Not grouped'.
The strategy is to help finance teams pay on time and avoid late-payment penalties, and auditability and traceability are core product promises.

vendor_risk uses no LLM and is a rule on the predicted delay with thresholds > 30 and > 10. An invalid paid_date rejects the row with reason 'paid_date'. A vendor not in risk_by_vendor gets risk 'unknown'.
The entry is consistent with D-2026-050 (paid invoices excluded) and D-2026-044 (Decimal amounts). It is assumed to follow D-2026-031 (calendar days).
PROV-ACME-2026-11 replaces acme-text-2, deprecated on 2026-12-01, and changes the same function as CR-4.
REG-LPR-2026-4.2 defines Late as a payable more than 60 days past its due date that remains unpaid. This entry's overdue means more than 30 days past due.
The connector approved for this step is api:github, limited to GET requests, and the notification channel is still open, so the output file is the notification record.
Fitment verdict: Yes (recommended), reason code FIT-Y-ROADMAP, to be decided by the PM and Leadership.

open_questions: FQ-1: The roadmap says 'overdue payables', while the ticket says 'vendors that usually pay late' and 'chase them first'. In the agent's judgement this wording is ambiguous in an AP context. The verdict assumes the risk level helps AP managers decide which overdue payables to act on first. The PM or Leadership should confirm this at the gate.
FQ-2: Keep 'overdue' (more than 30 days) and the regulatory 'Late' (more than 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2) as distinct labels.
FQ-3: Should org.strategy_capability be extended to cover ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_portal? Today it does not mention them.
FQ-4: Confirm that days past due in overdue_with_risk uses calendar days (D-2026-031), and test the boundary of exactly 30 days (L-007).
FQ-5: Is there an approved list of fitment reason codes? FIT-Y-ROADMAP is the agent's own code.
FQ-6: org.strategy_capability states no product out-of-scope list. Should one be added?
Carried forward from feat.classification: OQ-1 to OQ-5, and feat.prebacklog Q-1 to Q-5.
structured.summary: feat.fitment fixes the G1 refusal. The R-AP-12 link is no longer credited to REQ-02; the file now says feat.classification records the link and cites feat.prebacklog as its source. One more step-credit statement about ZD-48510 was reworded the same way. The recommendation is unchanged: Yes (FIT-Y-ROADMAP). The entry matches R-AP-12, builds on the ap_aging capability and supports both strategy statements, with no decision-log conflict. FQ-1, the business meaning of the ticket, goes to the PM and Leadership at the gate.
